'''Acid Cryptofiler''' is a cryptographic software program designed by the department for "control of information" (Centre d'Electronique de l'Armement) of the French General Directorate of Armament ([[Direction générale de l'armement]]).<ref>{{cite web|date=March 2011|title=CNRS Sécurité informatique n°11 march 2011|url=http://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/fsd/securite-systemes/revues-pdf/Si11.pdf|language=fr|access-date=August 11, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120815235502/http://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/fsd/securite-systemes/revues-pdf/Si11.pdf|archive-date=August 15, 2012}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine|last=Zetter|first=Kim|date=14 January 2013|title=Cybersleuths Uncover 5-Year Spy Operation Targeting Governments, Others|language=en-US|magazine=Wired|url=https://www.wired.com/2013/01/red-october-spy-campaign/|access-date=6 September 2021|issn=1059-1028}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last1=Pierre|first1=BARTHELEMY|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-4u9AgAAQBAJ&dq=%22Acid+Cryptofiler%22&pg=PA179|title=Cryptographie: principes et mises en œuvre / 2ème édition revue et augmentée|last2=Robert|first2=ROLLAND|last3=Pascal|first3=VERON|date=2012-04-16|publisher=Lavoisier|isbn=978-2-7462-8816-4|language=fr}}</ref> It is an online storage service.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|last1=Valeriano|first1=Brandon|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HuWkBwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Acid+Cryptofiler%22&pg=PA183|title=Cyber War versus Cyber Realities: Cyber Conflict in the International System|last2=Maness|first2=Ryan C.|date=2015-04-27|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-020480-8|language=en}}</ref>{{Contradict-inline|reason=An "online storage service" is different from a piece of software.|date=September 2021}} The software is now manufactured by ACID Technologies (France).<ref name=":0" />

== History ==
Acid Cryptofiler is on a list of cryptographic software approved for usage by the [[European Union]] and by the [[North Atlantic Treaty Organization]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=5 July 2021|title=List of approved cryptographic products (LACP) for protecting EU Classified Information (EUCI)|url=https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-5335-2021-REV-5/en/pdf|url-status=live|access-date=6 September 2021|website=data.consilium.europa.eu|format=PDF|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906054010/https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-5335-2021-REV-5/en/pdf |archive-date=2021-09-06 }}</ref> and is known to have been used by those organizations as well as by the [[European Parliament]] and [[European Commission]] since the summer of 2011.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=Storm|first=Darlene|date=2013-01-14|title=Red October 5-year cyber espionage attack: Malware resurrects itself|url=https://www.computerworld.com/article/2474163/red-october-5-year-cyber-espionage-attack--malware-resurrects-itself.html|access-date=2021-09-06|website=Computerworld|language=en}}</ref> It was approved for usage in the EU, in version V7, on 29 September 2011.<ref name=":0" />

In January 2013, as the [[Red October (malware)|Red October]] campaign was being discovered, researchers noted that the malware particularly targeted documents with ''.acid'' extensions, referring to documents processed by Acid Cryptofiler,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> including the file extensions ''acidcsa, acidsca, aciddsk, acidpvr, acidppr,'' and ''acidssa''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Unknown hackers stealing EU files for past five years|url=https://euobserver.com/institutional/118729|access-date=2021-09-06|website=EUobserver|date=14 January 2013 |language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
Acid Cryptofiler is based on the integration of government cryptographic libraries, including a CCSD [[Application programming interface|API]] (CCSD means "Defense Security Cryptographic Layers"). It offers the following functions:

* Asymmetric encryption (cf. [[public-key cryptography]]) in archive format (multi-file, multi-recipient) called Acid Archives.
* Volume encryption (containers) in symmetric mode and asymmetric mode.

Acid Cryptofiler is delivered with a directory function to file public keys, that is compliant with [[LDAP]] and [[Active Directory]].

A bunch file contains all public keys held by a user. A user can belong to different cryptographic domains (a domain is a CCSD library and a set of cryptographic parameters). Private keys are also stored in a bunch file.

The keys are generated by a centralized office under the responsibility of the [[chief information security officer]]. Before a user is given a key (or a pair of keys), he/she must be trusted by the centralized office.{{Citation needed|date=September 2021}} In France, Acid Cryptofiler does not fit for defense classified information.<ref name=":1" />{{Verify source|date=September 2021}}

Acid Cryptofiler was designed and developed by {{Citation needed span|text=two military engineers of|date=September 2021}} the [[Direction générale de l'armement]].<ref name=":1" /> {{Citation needed span|text=It has been delivered since 1999 (version 4, 5, and 7).|date=September 2021}}. It runs on [[Microsoft Windows]].<ref name=":1" /> The software is classified.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Walker|first=Danielle|date=15 January 2013|title="Red October" spy campaign uncovered, rivals Flame virus|url=http://www.scmagazine.com/red-october-spy-campaign-uncovered-rivals-flame-virus/printarticle/276016/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151009233555/http://www.scmagazine.com/red-october-spy-campaign-uncovered-rivals-flame-virus/printarticle/276016|archive-date=9 October 2015|access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref>

According to a book by [[Gérald Bronner]], Acid Cryptofiler was so slow that sending an email took 10 minutes.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bronner|first=Gérald|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oy-ODwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Acid+Cryptofiler%22&pg=PT61|title=Déchéance de rationalité: Les tribulations d'un homme de progrès dans un monde devenu fou|date=2019-03-20|publisher=Grasset|isbn=978-2-246-81281-4|language=fr}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2021|reason=Not sure if this is nonfiction.}}
